_about: Questions that need a research-style answer, each split by hand into the parts a planner should find. 'any' lists what a passage must contain to answer that part, and 'doc' limits it to the right document. Labels were written from the documents' text, before any search ran on them. A hand-written split is cleaner than a model's, so this measures the search method, not the planner.

questions.q: What is the Annadatha Sukhibhava scheme in Andhra Pradesh, who gets it, who is left out, how much is paid, and what did it replace?
questions.passage: The Annadatha Sukhibhava - PM Kisan scheme provides financial assistance to land owner farmer families and landless tenant farmer families per annum, payable in installments through the destination bank, subject to the exclusion criteria applicable to farmers of higher economic status.

questions.q: Explain crop insurance in Andhra Pradesh in detail: what do I pay, who can enrol, which risks are not covered, how are claims settled, and what changed from the free scheme?
questions.passage: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana notified by the State Government, farmers including tenant farmers may enrol voluntarily for notified crops on payment of the farmer's share of premium on the sum insured. Claims are assessed on yield data from Crop Cutting Experiments. Losses arising from war and nuclear risks are excluded.

questions.q: What is PM-KISAN, how much money do farmers get, who is not eligible, how do I register and what can I do if my installment does not come?
questions.passage: Under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, an amount per year is released by the Central Government directly into the bank accounts of landholding farmer families in three equal installments. Institutional land holders and families of higher economic status are excluded. Farmers may register through Common Service Centres and raise grievances with the Help Desk.

questions.q: Compare PMFBY and the weather based crop insurance RWBCIS: how losses are measured, what the farmer pays, and what add-on covers exist.
questions.passage: Unlike PMFBY, which is based on yield indices from Crop Cutting Experiments, RWBCIS uses weather parameters such as rainfall, temperature, wind speed and humidity as a proxy for crop yields. Farmers pay a share of premium on the sum insured. Add-on coverage may be notified by the State.

questions.q: How does a Kisan Credit Card work? Who can get one, how is the limit worked out, what interest is charged, what is the repayment incentive and how long is it valid?
questions.passage: The Kisan Credit Card scheme provides short term credit to owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees and share croppers. The limit is fixed on the scale of finance for the crop. Short term loans carry interest subvention, and a prompt repayment incentive is allowed to farmers who repay on time. The card is valid for five years.

questions.q: A seed dealer sold me bad seeds. What does the law say about dealer licences, penalties, and who can inspect or act?

questions.q: What rights do tenant farmers have in Andhra Pradesh under the Crop Cultivator Rights rules? How long is the agreement, which benefits can they get, and do they get Annadatha Sukhibhava?
questions.passage: Under the Andhra Pradesh Crop Cultivator Rights Rules, the land owner and the cultivator execute an agreement for a period of eleven months, countersigned by the Village Revenue Officer. The cultivator is entitled to obtain crop loans, crop insurance, input subsidy and crop damage compensation.

questions.q: My crop was destroyed in a flood in Andhra Pradesh. What input subsidy can I get, at what rates, what is the minimum loss, and how is relief sanctioned?
questions.passage: Input subsidy is provided for crops damaged by more than 33 percent due to a notified natural calamity, at the rates per hectare in the norms of assistance from the SDRF and NDRF. Enumeration of crop damage is taken up and the list of beneficiaries displayed before sanction of relief.

questions.q: Explain the subsidy for drip and sprinkler irrigation in Andhra Pradesh, including the central guidelines and what FRA patta holders get.
questions.topic: drip irrigation subsidy, APMIP and Per Drop More Crop
questions.passage: The Government approves the subsidy pattern for drip and sprinkler irrigation systems under the Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project. Assistance under Per Drop More Crop is 55 percent for small and marginal farmers and 45 percent for other farmers. FRA patta holders in identified districts receive enhanced subsidy.

questions.q: What is PM Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana? Who can join, how much is the contribution, what pension do I get, and what happens if I exit early?
questions.passage: The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for small and marginal farmers in the entry age group of 18 to 40 years, providing an assured monthly pension after 60 years. Subscribers make a monthly contribution matched by the Central Government. Co-contributions are not paid in case of premature exit.

questions.q: How does Atal Pension Yojana work? Who can join, what pension do I get, and can income tax payers join?
questions.passage: Atal Pension Yojana is a guaranteed pension scheme for citizens aged 18 to 40 years with a savings bank account. Subscribers receive a fixed monthly pension after the age of 60 depending on their contribution. Income tax payers are not eligible to join.
